objects_built.name: approvals
objects_built.role: Records each human-approved action on a target (action, target, status, requested_by, approved_by). Read by require_approval; nothing in the build writes approved rows.

objects_built.name: require_approval
objects_built.role: Stops with precondition unless an approvals row with status approved exists for the given action and target. Enforces the human-approval gate before email.

objects_changed.name: send_customer_email
objects_changed.change: Added function.run require_approval (action send_customer_email, target = input.to) before util.send_email.

assumptions: The agent's current tool list minus delete_customer_note is the customer's explicit approval, so issue_refund is approved.
require_approval is a precondition on an approvals row with status approved; the approver-vs-requester check was omitted.
Tool-level email and delete rules are what 'agents' means; an agent calling a non-tool function is covered only if the tool's stack reaches it.
Policies left advisory and active, since the skill says a new policy is advisory unless the owner chooses blocking.
Object files were written without guid lines; dry run accepted them.
confusions: The skill's recipe for AI agents says the approval function is required 'before every delete and email', but the stack.statement_order check only tests placement inside one stack. It was unclear whether it follows called functions; I did not verify that.

The template table's AI-001 fill says tools or tool_tags; the recipe also suggests tool_tags agent-approved. Unclear whether to tag tools or list names when the ask does not name the approved set; I chose the name list to avoid editing tags.
Whether a new policy's tags = [] is needed; the parser dropped it from output. Unclear whether omitting tags is the default.
No example in the skill shows a precondition or function.run shape for a required-approval gate; I copied function.run from account_DELETE.xs and precondition from login_POST.xs.
The skill says an extra_rule can use either AI-agent rules over tool stacks or agent settings; it did not say how an agent's own enabled-tool list interacts with a tool-stack rule.
wished_for: A worked recipe for 'human approves before the AI acts' that includes the approval table, the function, the approver-is-not-requester check, and the approval endpoint.
A note on whether stack.statement_order and stack.statement_forbidden follow function.run calls and at what depth.
A dry-run or evaluate hint on whether a function not yet on the branch satisfies a rule after push; the parser warning was clear but the consequence was not stated.
parse_errors_seen: Rule warning AGENT-GUARD.R2: Function require_approval is not on this branch (expected: created in this change)
why_confidence: Deletes by agent tools are forbidden and email from tools needs a require_approval call before it, both verified only as dry-run and parse, not evaluated. Approval is only checked as a row's existence, nothing writes approved rows yet, and the policies are advisory. The tool allowlist is only as strong as the list the customer confirms.
